paras: The killing of an unnamed Black man in Madison Parish, Louisiana, took place in or before June 1888, after a resident named T. H. Iler captured him on an accusation of robbery. Iler was charged with the killing and acquitted after a trial in Vicksburg, having claimed that two unknown men lynched the man.

According to the only report found, the man, described as "a negro," was said to have robbed Iler's house of $112. Evidence given at a preliminary trial was reported to show that he had also attempted to assault Iler's wife after the robbery.

Iler followed the man and captured him. By Iler's own account, he was on his way back with his prisoner when "two unknown men lynched the negro." The report gives no date, place or method for the killing and does not name the two men.

Iler was charged with killing the man, and after a preliminary hearing his case went to trial in Vicksburg. He was acquitted, and no report of an arrest or charge against anyone else appears in the coverage.

The episode survives in a single unheadlined paragraph in the Richland Beacon of June 23, 1888, a Louisiana weekly, which reported the acquittal rather than the killing itself. The paragraph stated the robbery as what "the negro had" done and the attempted assault as what the preliminary evidence showed, while presenting the lynching only as Iler's claim. It offered no comment on the killing or the verdict.
No other newspaper report of the killing, its inquest or the trial was found.

reader.title: Killing of an unnamed Black man in Madison Parish, Louisiana (1888)
bases: A1 reports that a captured Black man accused of robbery was killed and that his captor, charged with the killing, claimed 'two unknown men lynched the negro'; the paper itself uses the word lynched only as the captor's claim.

A1 shows a Black man accused of robbery and attempted assault was killed without legal process after capture, but the only account of who killed him is the claim of the accused captor, T. H. Iler, that two unknown men did it, while Iler himself was charged; no source shows a group of three or more.
Only one brief item (A1), published after the acquittal, reports the episode; no first report of the killing was found.

accounts.label: Iler's claim
accounts.gist: Iler said he had followed and captured the man and was returning with him when two unknown men lynched him.

accounts.label: Preliminary-trial evidence
accounts.gist: Evidence at the preliminary trial was reported to show that the man had attempted to assault Iler's wife after robbing the house.

framing.detail: The Richland Beacon ran a short unheadlined paragraph reporting the acquittal, stating the robbery as fact ('It seems the negro had robbed Iler's house') and attributing the lynching to Iler's claim.

sources.note: Only report found: T. H. Iler of Madison parish acquitted at Vicksburg of killing a negro he had captured after a robbery of his house; Iler claimed two unknown men lynched the man.
quotes: T. H. Iler, of Madison parish was charged with killing a negro, but after a trial in Vicksburg, was acquitted.
Iler had followed the negro, captured him and was on his return, when he, Iler, claims that two unknown men lynched the negro.
From the evidence adduced on the preliminary trial the negro attempted to assault Iler's wife after robbing the house.
